Good morning. Before we open the dashboard, three things about the quarter. Turnover is at fourteen point two percent, which is one point six points higher than last quarter and the highest figure in three years. Absenteeism is steady at three point eight percent, so that one is not our problem right now. Overtime is where the money is: we paid one point four million dollars in extra hours, and forty per cent of that comes from two sites only. If you break the turnover number down by area, operations is at nineteen percent and the corporate offices are at six. So we do not have a company problem. We have a problem in two buildings, and the average is hiding it.

Hi Adriana, it is Monica from the benchmark team. I am sending the comparison you asked for. The market average for your sector is eleven point five percent, so you are almost three points above it, and the gap is wider in operations than anywhere else. One thing before you present this: our data covers companies of the same size, but half of them are in the north of the country, where the labor market is much tighter. So the benchmark is useful, but it is not a verdict. If anybody in the room says your number is bad, ask them which companies they are comparing you with. Call me if you want the breakdown by region.
